C-RECOVER-FOLDABLE.IntentSummary: Close F13 so recover --fix produces a foldable ledger: extend the *effective* covering allocation by appending a superseding opened/Allocation (D9 append-only, D9.1 name stays extend-allocation and becomes true), teach fold/diagnose to validate only live (non-superseded) ranges, repair the damaged C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY shape on a copy, and prove clean and damaged paths end-to-end without a pre-seeded terminal. Emitting terminal remains the operator's act (F12 / A29.2). Live ledgers are not mutated by implementation; authority applies the repair afterward.

T-001.Title: Effective allocation supersession and honest extend-allocation (F13 / D9 / D9.1)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: on a temp run/ with loose integer events, no terminal, and either no Allocation or only a dead closed-ceiling Allocation that does not cover a later event, recover --fix today either leaves fold blocked after an operator terminal (F13) or leaves a prior range unterminated under per-allocation validation — capture that failure mode in a regression that fails on pre-fix code (assert via recover diagnosis foldBlocked / foldEpoch throw, not a private helper alone).

After fix: recover --fix appends a new kind=opened event with Allocation; it never rewrites any existing run/* event file (D9). The new Allocation's derived bounds make the *effective* covering range include every loose integer id after the write (including the new opened id) — the covering requirement. The ceiling is max(covering requirement, openedId + 98), matching the --open-epoch default (to = from + 98). When a terminal already exists among loose events, the covering requirement includes that terminal id; max(..., openedId + 98) still applies. writeCoveringOpened is the single covering-write path: maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation and recover --fix share that function, so auto-open inherits the same headroom and covering-requirement rules with no carve-out.

foldEpoch and recover diagnose validate membership, density, and terminal only against the effective allocation set (per worker: Allocation on the highest-id kind=opened that declares one for that worker — last-writer-wins; the whole supersession rule). Superseded (older) Allocations for the same worker are not checked for termination and are not written as Epoch-level Allocation nodes into run-ledger.xml. Discriminating negative: a change that makes fold ignore unterminated ranges for *all* allocations — including a sole live range with no terminal — fails this criterion; termination remains required for every live effective range.

Flag honesty (D9.1 / AC-FIX-FLAG-HONESTY): the --fix operation remains named extend-allocation; CLI help and library docs state that it extends the effective covering allocation by appending a superseding opened/Allocation. Behaviour matches that name. Assert via CLI help text or documented option description plus behavioural tests a reviewer can run.

Carried constraints (AC-CARRIED-ORPHAN-WORKER-A29) — assert, do not only name: (D8.3) on a fixture that includes an event-filename NaN-* orphan, after recover --fix the orphan still exists on disk and recover still diagnoses it as unrecoverable; after a subsequent successful fold of the valid stream the orphan still exists and is still diagnosed (fold deletes only listLooseEvents members). (D8.2) when more than one distinct worker value appears, recover --fix and auto-open refuse; multi-worker ranges are never fabricated — regression retained or reasserted under effective-allocation rules. (A29.2 / F12) recover --fix does not emit kind=terminal; the operator emits the terminal. A path that writes a terminal from --fix fails this criterion.

T-002.Title: Damaged-shape repair: dead allocation + outside terminal + NaN orphan

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: build a *copy* of C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY's current ledger shape — loose integer events 1..20, a dead Allocation w0:[1,19] on an opened event (no terminal in that range), a kind=terminal at id 20 outside every allocation, and a NaN-T-001-opened.xml event-filename orphan (content matching the live fixture shape; live file SHA-1 c0cc8899c264381766a18918e2109b5e05693893 is the reference for the orphan bytes when copying from the live tree). On that copy, before the fix, recover reports fold blocked (event 20 outside; unterminated range for w0) and foldEpoch fails — write that failing regression first.

After T-001's mechanism: recover --fix on that copy appends a superseding covering opened (ceiling max(covering requirement, openedId + 98)); effective allocation covers events 1..20 (and the new opened id); foldEpoch succeeds; the NaN-* orphan still exists on disk after --fix and after fold; recover still diagnoses it as an unrecoverable orphan. A design or test that only exercises a clean shape (no dead prior allocation) does not satisfy this criterion — preventing the defect on new ledgers alone fails AC-RECOVER-FIX-DAMAGED-SHAPE.

Carried constraints on this path (AC-CARRIED-ORPHAN-WORKER-A29): orphan survival after --fix and after fold as above (D8.3); --fix on this single-worker copy does not emit a terminal (A29.2 / F12) — the fixture already has operator terminal id 20, and --fix must not add another; multi-worker refuse (D8.2) remains true of the shared recover/auto-open path (asserted in T-001; this task must not weaken it). Tests never mutate the live C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY or C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY ledgers. Repairing and folding the real C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY run/ remains a separate authorized act by the authority after this bundle lands — not this task.

T-003.Title: Clean no-terminal E2E, suite close, no withTerminal pre-seed

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first then green: a run/ with loose integer events, no valid covering allocation, and **no terminal event anywhere** (and no withTerminal seed or equivalent), after recover --fix (covering ceiling max(requirement, openedId + 98)), operator cursor advance --kind terminal (and any intervening progress/attempt within that headroom), and cursor fold, the epoch folds successfully; any NaN-* (or event-filename) orphan present before the sequence still exists on disk after --fix and after fold and is still diagnosed. Assert through foldEpoch applied / CLI fold and recover diagnosis, not internal helpers alone. --fix must not have emitted the terminal (A29.2 / F12) — the operator event is required and distinct.

AC-REGRESSION-NO-PRESEEDED-TERMINAL: end-to-end coverage includes (1) the clean shape above and (2) the damaged-shape path from T-002. **Neither may be satisfied by seeding withTerminal: true or any equivalent that places a terminal inside the pre-fix id range** — that supplies the precondition under test (F12.1 / F13.1). A test that passes only because a terminal was present before --fix fails this criterion. Prior orphan-survival assertions from C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY remain green; the fold-succeeds half is proven by these no-preseeded-terminal paths.

Carried constraints (AC-CARRIED-ORPHAN-WORKER-A29) on the suite surface: orphan non-deletion after --fix and after fold retained; multi-worker refuse for recover --fix and auto-open retained under effective-allocation rules (D8.2); no path under recover --fix emits kind=terminal (A29.2 / F12).
